versions.notes:
The interior of the gatefold sleeve features original session photography of the musicians. The first 1000 copies were numbered with a silver sticker on the back cover, with the remaining copies being unnumbered. The generic series sticker on the front of the outer bag hypes mastering by "Kevin Gray & Steve Hoffman" but on this release only [a312098]'s initials are etched in the runouts.

Track durations are not printed on the release.

versions.title: Conference Of The Birds
versions.notes:
From front inlay: "While living in London I had an apartement with a small garden. During the summer around 4 or 5 o'clock in the morning, just as the day began, birds would gather here one by one and sing together, each declaring its freedom in song. It is my wish to share this same spirit with other musicians and communicate it to the people. - David Holland"

Recorded on November 30, 1972 at Allegro Studio, New York City

versions.notes:
"One of the most original talents to emerge from the jazz avant garde of the 1960s, Sam Rivers is best known as a saxophonist of striking lyricism and power. This 1974 orchestral session offers a showcase for his equally impressive skills as a composer and arranger."

Recorded March 4, 1974.

Comes in a mini-LP with a OBI (as per LP Reproduction series).
"96 kHz, 24-bit digital transfer
Available until September 2005"

Printed in USA.

C3 recorded live on July 6, 1973 at The Montreux Jazz Festival, Montreux, Switzerland.
C4, C5 recorded live on October 27, 1972 at Oakland University, Rochester, Michigan.
Side D recorded live on August 3, 1973, at the Molde Jazz Festival, Molde, Norway.

Side B is released in its entity here for the first time.

versions.title: Dimensions & Extensions
versions.notes:
Recorded at the Van Gelder Studio, Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey on March 17, 1967.

Note: This material was previously released in 1976 as part of a double album Involution (BN-LA453-H2). It is now issued here, for the first time, with the cover art and catalogue number, as originally intended by Blue Note in 1967.

The classic Blue Note albums which span the mid 1950's to late 1960's were recorded directly on to two track analog tape. No multitrack recording was used and consequently no mixing was required. Therefore, this CD was made by transferring the one step analog master to digital.

Note: This material was previously released in 1976 as part of a double album Involution (BN-LA453-H2). It is now issued here, for the first time, with the cover art and catalogue number, as originally intended by Blue Note in 1967.

The classic Blue Note albums which span the mid 1950's to late 1960's were recorded directly on to two track analog tape. No multitrack recording was used and consequently no mixing was required. Therefore, this CD was made by transferring the one step analog master to digital.

versions.notes:
There are numerous typos and outright errors on this CD edition.
Track 3 should read The Soulful Mr. Timmons and it was written by James Williams, not Art Blakey, as shown on the tray card.
Track 4 is listed as My Ideal, though it is obviously Au Privave as shown on other editions.
Track 5, Free For All, was written by Wayne Shorter, not Frank Mitchell, as shown on the tray card.
The names of Richard Rodgers and Charlie Parker are also incorrect.

Original LP title from the sleeve is actually "Recorded Live At Bubba's Jazz Restaurant" and was recorded at Bubba's Jazz Restaurant in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, October 11, 1980. This is a 1988 CD reissue, which states made in Holland.
